sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Alter-ego reveal and sharing
sections.what: Checks the reveal stays locked until ten graded calls, then shows the label and axes, creates an opt-in share image that is a PNG, and confirms stopping sharing makes the link return not found.
sections.why: Confirms the profile unlocks on evidence, and that sharing is a deliberate and reversible choice.
sections.watch_out: The evidence branch writes files into the docs folder, and the test relies on a fixed count of ten calls.

summary: Browser test of the alter-ego reveal: the case file stays classified until ten graded calls, then reveals a label, five explained axes and an opt-in share card that can be revoked.
purpose: Confirms the reveal only unlocks after enough graded calls and that sharing is optional and reversible.
why: The reveal is a personal profile, so it must wait for enough evidence and must never be shared without a user's explicit action.
how: It creates a user and locks nine calls, then checks the dossier shows classified and one call to go. It locks a tenth call and checks the dossier shows revealed, a label matching one of the five personas with one of five styles, and five axis descriptions including risk appetite, and the provisional label. It clicks share, checks the share link has the expected form, fetches the image and checks it is a PNG. It optionally saves screenshots, runs an accessibility check, stops sharing, and checks the old link now returns 404.
inputs: A new user, ten fixture moments, and the alter-ego page.
outputs: Pass or fail for each stage, plus optional screenshots and a saved card image.
risks: When the evidence setting is on, the test writes screenshots and a card image into the evidence folder. Expected persona and style names are fixed.
debug: Check the dossier's call count if the reveal unlocks at the wrong time. If the share link fails, check that stopping sharing actually removes it.
